contract: An interface export is ONE quantity for every interface it monitors, named on the file's title line: "Interface Hourly 'Power Flow (MW)' Data for Year 2034". So the aggregation rule is a property of the FILE, not of the column, and it is resolved from the unit in that title. `temporal` is the only rule left: interfaces are never summed across each other (a path total is not a quantity anyone asked for), so there is no spatial rule to get wrong. SUM means a period total over the filtered hours is meaningful; MEAN means it is not, and the stats table shows no total at all rather than a plausible wrong one. Resolution: exact match on `unit` (case-sensitive), else no rule -- an unrecognised unit gets MEAN and no total, never a guess.

units.note: MW is a rate. Summing it over hours produces neither MW nor MWh once a filter has removed hours from the interval, so no total is offered.
A price is intensive: the sum of hourly prices is not a price. The mean over the kept hours is the unweighted mean of the hours themselves.
